records.head: 96a5718f8e8b28a4e30af0211f2d7ab6ac1cf9bd
records.title: Match legacy JavaScript MIME types exactly in HTML inventories (R3.13)
records.body:
## Problem

The HTML script scanner accepts any suffix beginning with `1` after eight JavaScript MIME types. For example, `text/javascript1evil` and `application/javascript1.0` become executable scripts in the inventory even though browsers treat them as data. Inline blocks then contribute false application endpoints, and external blocks create false page imports and execution roles.

## Change

Match the six legacy types `text/javascript1.0` through `text/javascript1.5` exactly. The other standard JavaScript MIME types retain exact, ASCII case-insensitive matching.

The existing module, Babel/JSX, empty-type and MIME-parameter policies remain. Unsupported types still consume their whole script block, so the next real script keeps its byte range and line. Application tests also retain facts from an explicitly supplied standalone data.js file while removing its false page import.

The exact legacy list follows [WHATWG MIME Sniffing §4.6](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type). This change does not expand into the scanner's intentional Babel/JSX or parameter handling.

Roadmap: R3.13. Public claim `2226d2e` preceded implementation; the branch is based on upstream `7116cc6`.

## Validation

- Original source: **6 regression failures and 4 passing controls** across the public scanner and application graph.
- All **10 new regression groups** pass. The complete JavaScript and analysis suites pass: **250 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**, across 31 test targets including doc-test targets.
- Real Chromium **158.0.8127.18** executes 16 standard JavaScript MIME fixtures and leaves ten unsupported suffix fixtures inert. Original scanner: 26 scripts, including all ten false positives. Fixed scanner: exactly the same 16 scripts Chromium executed.
- Strict all-target Clippy, workspace formatting, layer/lock checks, secret scanning, all L0–L2 WebAssembly gates and an unchanged source tree pass with Rust 1.99.
- The first full run caught a test-fixture expectation of `renderer` where the existing ordinary-web contract is `page`. Only that test name and role assertion were corrected; product code was unchanged. The failed run remains available.

[Original Chromium comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43036021283/job/130574918129) · [Complete fixed validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43038199945/job/130582606184) · [Initial fixture diagnostic](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43037534160/job/130580258150)

The complete suite validates `065ee639`. Final head `96a5718f` changes only ROADMAP and STATUS; a separate fixed-head check verifies every implementation, test and dependency file is identical, and repeats formatting, secret scanning and diff checks.

[Final documentation and identity check](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43038999162/job/130585447800)

records.head: b2852f5be20729800dbda67286324ac2e48cb8cb
records.title: Preserve literal values and tree boundaries in JavaScript fingerprints (R3.12)
records.body:
## Problem

Structural fingerprints omit BigInt values, regular-expression patterns and flags, and template text. They also concatenate unframed string contents and record only entry into syntax nodes. Different programs can therefore share a fingerprint: `["a", "b"]` collides with `["a\0StringLiteral;b"]`, and `[[], []]` collides with `[[[]]]`.

Application comparisons can pair different files as structural renames or omit changed bundle modules. Correcting the encoding also needs an explicit compatibility boundary for retained application graphs.

## Change

Include exact parsed BigInt values, regular-expression patterns and flag sets, and every template element's raw text. Give string and other variable-length payloads a byte-length prefix, and mark each syntax-node exit so sibling and nested trees remain distinct.

Equivalent BigInt spellings, regular-expression flag order, equivalent string and number spellings, and identifier renaming still match. Tagged templates retain observable raw escapes, including escapes without a cooked value.

**Every parsed fingerprint changes with the new encoding.** Fresh application graphs record fingerprint version 1. A missing version is legacy version 0. Both retained-graph comparison tools require both inputs to use the current version; legacy and unknown future versions receive a clear instruction to run `js_app_map` again on both original inputs. Older graphs remain readable for unrelated inspection. The public L2 comparison functions document the same precondition.

Roadmap: R3.12. Original public claim `dfd752af` preceded the literal implementation; expanded claim `95d38566` preceded the framing and retained-version changes. This remains one improvement on the independently based `22c44d01` branch.

## Validation

- Original fingerprint implementation with the current regression fixtures: **8 failures and 7 passing controls**. The previous prepared head's fingerprint implementation reproduces **4 failures and 11 passing controls**.
- Original engine comparison entry points, with valid retained evidence and the new tool tests: **1 failing regression group and 6 passing controls**. Legacy/legacy and future/future pairs are rejected along with mixed versions; current retained evidence and direct paths compare successfully, and unrelated legacy-graph inspection remains available.
- Fixed code: all **18 focused regression groups** pass. Complete JavaScript, analysis and engine suites: **936 passed, 0 failed, 7 existing ignored**, across **51 targets** including doc tests.
- Actual Node **22.23.4** execution of **17 program pairs**: 11 different runtime results and 6 equivalent controls. Fixed fingerprints distinguish all 11 changes, each changed webpack module is reported, and all equivalent file/module pairs still match. An earlier native probe independently reproduced both framing collisions on the previous ready head.
- Strict all-target Clippy for all three touched crates, workspace formatting, layer/lock checks, secret scanning, all L0–L2 WebAssembly checks and an unchanged source tree pass with Rust 1.99.
- The first expanded validation run stopped at formatting in three test layouts. The formatter-only follow-up changed neither production logic nor assertions; the complete successful run uses tested head `7d3dd731`.

[Original literal runtime comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43039360696/job/130586691737) · [Previous-head framing collision probe](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43049841226/job/130623606411) · [Complete expanded validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43053715982/job/130637465068)

Final head `b2852f5b` changes only ROADMAP and STATUS after the tested head. A separate fixed-head check verifies every implementation, test and dependency file is identical, then repeats formatting, secret scanning and diff checks. The original public ready branch was advanced only after both checks completed successfully.

[Final documentation and identity check](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43055905929/job/130645169385)

records.head: 4e5db9ce57cd4c14d918b6612b844a54f47b79f8
records.title: Preserve boundary escapes in reference-source ignore rules (R3.12)
records.body:
## Problem

The ignore-rule reader removes a leading backslash before its tokenizer sees it and trims all trailing whitespace. As a result, `\*.js` excludes ordinary JavaScript files, a quoted trailing space matches the wrong filename, and a trailing incomplete escape can silently become a valid rule. These decisions feed the source-tree walk and alter which reference files enter analysis.

## Change

Keep leading escapes for the existing tokenizer to consume once. Split lines at LF, remove one optional ending CR, and trim only unescaped ASCII spaces. Literal tabs, non-breaking spaces and quoted trailing spaces remain part of a pattern.

An unmatched terminal backslash makes a rule invalid, including a negated rule. Ordinary glob matching, anchoring, directory-only rules, negation and nested ignore-file bases retain their behavior.

The boundary handling follows the [Git ignore pattern format](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore), with the exact results checked against native Git. The implementation is original and introduces no dependency.

Roadmap: R3.12. Public claim `640d5c0a` preceded implementation. The branch is independently based on `22c44d01`.

## Validation

- Original source: **7 regression failures and 2 passing controls**. All **9 public regression groups** pass with the fix.
- Complete analysis suite: **164 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**, across 19 targets including doc tests.
- Native **Git 2.56.0** on Linux, invoked through Node 22.23.4: 20 `.gitignore` fixtures and 54 real file paths. Original reader disagrees on **24 decisions**; the fixed reader agrees on **all 54**.
- The native comparison includes literal metacharacters and backslashes, quoted spaces with padding, incomplete positive/negative escapes, tabs, non-breaking spaces, CR/CRLF, a literal remaining CR, scoped rules and ordinary matching controls.
- Strict all-target analysis Clippy, workspace formatting, layer/lock checks, secret scanning, all L0–L2 WebAssembly gates and an unchanged source tree pass with Rust 1.99.

[Original Git comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43041348554/job/130593663456) · [Full fixed validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43042736484/job/130598528151)

The complete suite validates `debc7600`. Final head `4e5db9ce` changes only ROADMAP and STATUS. The final-head check verifies every implementation, test and dependency file is identical, then repeats formatting, secret scanning and diff checks.

[Final documentation and identity check](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43044757894/job/130605648002)

records.head: 625490640c47196eb5c51343b9f08cd3c9623788
records.title: Preserve GraphQL operations containing escaped block-string quotes (R3.11)
records.body:
## Problem

The GraphQL operation reader closes a block string at the first three quotes, including the escaped triple-quote sequence that belongs to the string's contents. Valid operations can disappear from API inventories, and an unterminated block can be reported as a valid operation.

The shared reader handles both operation headers and selection sets, so this affects variable defaults, directive arguments, fragment contents and ordinary field arguments in both parsed-source and fallback analysis.

## Change

Consume the block-string escape as one literal triple quote and reset the pending quote count. Backslashes that precede other text remain literal, including earlier backslashes in a run. A block ends only at a genuine closing delimiter.

The change is confined to the shared block-string scanner. Public regressions cover query, mutation and subscription operations, later operations after fragments, Unicode and multiline content, adjacent quote runs, missing closers, parsed-source facts, fallback facts and ordinary-string controls. The reader remains a bounded structural recognizer rather than a complete validating GraphQL parser.

The block-string rule follows [GraphQL's String Value grammar](https://spec.graphql.org/September2025/#sec-String-Value). Production code and fixtures are original.

Roadmap: R3.11. Claim `9770c5ae` was published before implementation. Base: `3a9ad9c6`.

## Validation

- Unchanged production source with the new public regression file: **8 failures and 2 passing controls**. The workflow asserts the exact failure set.
- Revised regression file: **10 groups pass**.
- Complete JavaScript and analysis suites: **254 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored across 31 test targets**, including doc tests.
- Node 22.23.4 with GraphQL.js 16.11.0 parses the same **25 valid and 7 invalid documents**. Across the direct reader, parsed-source analysis and fallback analysis, the unchanged source has **69 mismatches across 23 documents**; the revised source has **0 mismatches across all 96 comparisons**. Nine documents already agree on the baseline.
- Strict all-target Clippy for both crates, workspace formatting, layer and lock checks, secret scan, all L0–L2 WebAssembly builds and clean-tree checks pass with Rust 1.99.
- Final head `62549064` changes only ROADMAP and STATUS relative to the fully tested implementation `cfbaa14a`. A separate frozen-head run confirms every implementation, test and dependency file is identical, then reruns formatting, the secret scan and diff checks.

Evidence:
- [Native unchanged-source comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43047974989/job/130616967500)
- [Negative controls, complete suites, native comparison and repository gates](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43048431504/job/130618613367)
- [Final-document and implementation identity checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43049563657/job/130622636246)

The [first diagnostic run](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43047446445/job/130615055636) incorrectly compared JSON object serialization order. The diagnostic was changed to structural equality without changing production source or fixtures; the corrected baseline and fixed comparisons above retain that distinction.

records.head: 525951df9541dd8a95d4c5bfa91c2ce3b8d8612c
records.title: Avoid quadratic scans in reference-source ignore matching (R3.12)
records.body:
## Problem

For every pathname position, the `**/` token scans the remaining suffix again to find a matching slash boundary. An unmatched rule therefore does quadratic work as paths grow. This cost is paid while importing reference source trees and can repeat for every ignore rule and source file.

## Change

Carry a suffix-match flag while visiting the pathname backwards. Each position contributes its slash-boundary match once; the flag is reset for each pattern token. The empty-directory alternative still reads the next token row directly.

The change keeps the existing matcher structure and allocation bounds. Public controls cover zero and multiple directories, component boundaries, repeated globstars, ordinary wildcards and character classes, ordered negations, nested ignore files, Unicode and long paths.

Roadmap: R3.12. Claim `be6534f1` was published before implementation. The branch is based on `adeddc91`.

## Validation

- All **8 public compatibility groups pass on both the original and revised matcher**.
- Complete analysis suite: **164 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored across 19 test targets**, including doc tests.
- Both implementations match Git 2.56.0 on the same **240 pattern/path comparisons**. The native oracle creates and reads **52 actual files**, including deep paths below Linux's pathname limit.
- On one Ubuntu 24.04 runner with Rust 1.99, the analysis crate's matcher compiled at optimization level 3. Each table entry is the median of three samples of **200 public `Ignore::is_ignored` calls** for one unmatched `**/never.js` rule:

| Relative pathname bytes | Original | Revised | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 609 | 29.917 ms | 3.123 ms | 9.6× |
| 1,209 | 109.344 ms | 5.948 ms | 18.4× |
| 2,409 | 419.532 ms | 11.816 ms | 35.5× |
| 3,609 | 948.990 ms | 17.568 ms | 54.0× |

These measurements isolate ignore matching on the recorded inputs. They show the avoided suffix rescans; complete source-import speed also depends on file reading and parsing.

- Strict all-target analysis Clippy, workspace formatting, layer and lock checks, secret scan, all L0–L2 WebAssembly builds and clean-tree checks pass.
- Final head `525951df` changes only ROADMAP and STATUS relative to tested `422bbdca`. The final frozen-head run confirms every implementation, test and dependency file is identical, then reruns formatting, the secret scan and diff checks.

Evidence:
- [Initial native Git and optimized-matcher baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43048933349/job/130620444100)
- [Same-run original/revised measurements, full suite and repository gates](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43051956453/job/130631191804)
- [Final-document and implementation identity checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43053565395/job/130636923199)

The first full run stopped at formatting. Its follow-up only compacted one test call; production code and assertions were unchanged before the successful complete run above.
